summary: Pilot sketch of Rooth's alternative semantics (1985, 1992) extended to Greek additive/exclusive operators (ke, mono) following an unidentified 'CSM&S' analysis: possible-worlds propositions, alternative sets as lists, pointwise application, a squiggle-style focus_interp, only/too semantics, a sisterhood-flagged mono/ke, Link-style DIST/COLL over parametric sum entities, a distributive-to-additive diachronic hypothesis as an unproved definition, and a toy syntactic-position table. The alternative-set generators are singleton stubs (the file's own comments say 'should be proper alternative set'), the FocusOperator record is uninhabited (its focus_sensitivity condition is self-contradictory at C = [p]), ke_conjunction's collective disjunct is trivially true (witness fun _ _ => True), and the single theorem (mono_ke_movement_asymmetry) is true by unfolding a hand-coded can_move table.

sources.citation: Rooth, M. (1985). Association with Focus. PhD dissertation, UMass Amherst.
Rooth, M. (1992). A theory of focus interpretation. Natural Language Semantics 1:75-116.

'CSM&S' (cited only as such in the file's comments): analysis of Greek mono/ke with a sisterhood constraint on focus association, a mono-vs-ke movement asymmetry, and the hypothesis that additive ke arose from distributive ke misapplied to singulars; plausibly Spathas and colleagues on focus in Modern Greek, but the citation could not be verified and no PDF is in the papers directory.

definitions_mapped.coq: Proposition := World -> Prop; Parameters Entity, World
definitions_mapped.source: Rooth's possible-worlds propositions over a domain of entities
definitions_mapped.note: signature Parameters only, no propositional content

definitions_mapped.coq: AlternativeSet A := list A; alt / entity_alternatives / prop_alternatives
definitions_mapped.source: Rooth's focus semantic value: the set of alternatives obtained by substituting objects of matching type for the focused constituent
definitions_mapped.note: degenerate: all three generators return the singleton of the ordinary value regardless of focus marking; the file's own comments admit 'Simplified - should be proper alternative set'. Focus value = {ordinary value} always, so focus is semantically inert

definitions_mapped.source: Hamblin/Rooth pointwise functional application of alternative sets

definitions_mapped.coq: focus_interp C p := In p C
definitions_mapped.source: Rooth 1992's squiggle operator ~ (presupposes C is a subset of the focus value and contains the ordinary value)
definitions_mapped.note: reduced to bare list membership stated as an ordinary Prop; no presupposition, no subset-of-focus-value constraint
UNINHABITED: taking C = [p], focus_interp holds by In, and the field then demands operator_meaning [p] p <> operator_meaning [p] p, which is contradictory; no instance is (or can be) constructed

definitions_mapped.source: Roothian 'only' (prejacent + exclusion of alternatives) and additive 'too' (prejacent + a distinct true alternative)
definitions_mapped.note: presuppositions flattened into truth-conditional conjuncts; alternative distinctness/exclusion via intensional inequality q <> p on World -> Prop functions

definitions_mapped.source: CSM&S sisterhood constraint on Greek association with focus
definitions_mapped.note: a syntactic well-formedness condition is encoded as a boolean flag inside the truth conditions; failure of association denotes the false proposition

definitions_mapped.coq: Parameters SumEntity, atom, sum; DIST; COLL; ke_conjunction; ke_double
definitions_mapped.source: Link-style plural semantics behind distributive ke...ke vs plain ke conjunction
definitions_mapped.note: no mereological axioms (atom/sum are bare signatures); ke_conjunction's collective disjunct 'exists P_sum, COLL P_sum sum_e w' is trivially true (witness fun _ _ => True), so plain-ke conjunction denotes the trivially true proposition; ke_double (DIST only) is the sensible half

definitions_mapped.source: CSM&S hypothesis: distributive ke misapplied to singulars yields the additive reading
definitions_mapped.note: stated as an unproved Prop-valued definition, never asserted or established as a theorem; the headline diachronic claim is not formalized as a result

definitions_mapped.source: CSM&S syntactic distribution: mono can move, ke cannot; sisterhood positions
definitions_mapped.note: hand-coded finite lookup tables; the empirical content is stipulated, not derived

theorems.name: mono_ke_movement_asymmetry
theorems.source_claim: CSM&S's asymmetry that mono can move while additive ke cannot
theorems.note: trivial by unfolding the hand-coded can_move table (both conjuncts close by auto); under rubric section 3 the verifier would exclude it from substantive counts. The section-8 comment 'Alternative semantics provides proper focus sensitivity' is followed by no theorem — the intended headline result was never written. Classical_Prop and FunctionalExtensionality are imported but unused by the proof

evidence: The core construct of the source — the focus semantic value — is a singleton stub: alt returns cons s nil for both focused and unfocused input, and entity_alternatives/prop_alternatives likewise return singletons, with in-file comments conceding 'should be proper alternative set'; focus is therefore semantically inert, which is the negation of Rooth's theory.
The FocusOperator record meant to capture focus sensitivity is uninhabited: at C = cons p nil its focus_sensitivity field requires operator_meaning [p] p <> operator_meaning [p] p.
ke_conjunction's collective disjunct (exists P_sum, COLL P_sum sum_e w) is satisfied by fun _ _ => True at every world, making plain-ke conjunction trivially true.

The headline claims (focus sensitivity of alternative semantics; the distributive-to-additive development of ke) are stated only as a comment and an unproved definition; the sole Qed theorem verifies a hand-coded two-line movement table by unfolding.
simplifications: presuppositions of only/too rendered as truth-conditional conjuncts
sisterhood as a boolean flag inside truth conditions
alternative exclusion/distinctness via intensional inequality on World -> Prop functions
omissions: genuine alternative generation (substitution into the focused position)
any theorem about only/too semantics (entailments, additivity, projection)
the distributive-to-additive derivation as a proved result
additions: the SyntacticPosition inventory with sister/can_move lookup tables

determination_rationale: A determination must be evidenced by a formalization (rubric section 4); this file supplies none. It is a skeleton whose alternative sets are degenerate singletons, whose focus-operator abstraction is contradictory, and whose only theorem is a trivial table lookup the section-3 verifier would exclude — so it evidences neither 'as-is' nor any resistance of Rooth's theory ('we did not manage' is not 'cannot'). Rooth 1985/1992 and the CSM&S analysis remain effectively unassessed pending a real formalization; per section 1 they should carry only the survey category.

artifact_classes.description: missing native structure: no presupposition machinery (only/too presuppositions flattened to assertions), no syntax-semantics interface (sisterhood becomes a boolean flag whose failure denotes falsity), lists standing in for alternative sets, and Link mereology reduced to unaxiomatized Parameters

identity/decidability gap: alternative exclusion and distinctness hinge on intensional inequality q <> p between World -> Prop functions, which is neither decidable nor the semantic (truth-conditional) equivalence the source's set-of-alternatives talk presumes
